questions.question_text:
Match the strategy (irrigation, genetically modified crops, agricultural machinery) with its purpose:
1. provides water to dry areas
2. increases crop resistance and yields
3. improves efficiency in farming

keywords_required: Irrigation - provides water to dry areas
Genetically modified crops - increases crop resistance and yields
Agricultural machinery - improves efficiency in farming

questions.question_text: What does the 'globalisation of food supplies' mean? [2]

keywords_required: The increasing integration and trade of food products worldwide.
Consumers can buy out-of-season and exotic foods sourced from all over the world, rather than just locally grown produce.

questions.question_text: Justify the use of genetically modified (GM) crops to increase food supply. [3]

marking_scheme.rubric: AO2 and Exam Skills: Provide justification for GM crops.
keywords_required: GM crops can be engineered to be resistant to pests/diseases, reducing crop loss.
They can be designed to withstand extreme weather like drought, which is vital due to climate change.
They produce higher yields per hectare, which is essential to feed a rapidly growing global population.

questions.question_text: Study Figure 10.2 (calories map). Justify how increasing food production can help meet global demand. [3]

marking_scheme.rubric: AO2 and AO3: Justify increasing production.
keywords_required: The map shows clear regional disparities in calorie intake, with some LICs suffering from undernourishment.
Increasing production, especially locally in these deficit regions, ensures food security and reduces reliance on expensive imports.
As the global population approaches 10 billion, total caloric demand will skyrocket; production must increase to prevent widespread famine.
